- Pregnancy (due to known effects on refraction and visual acuity).

=### Study Title:
A Single-Site, Randomized, Contralateral Eye Trial Comparing Active Sentry at Low IOP vs Ozil at High IOP


### Study Design:
Single site, single-masked, randomized, prospective contralateral eye study.


### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint: The total aspiration time between groups on the day of surgery.  

Secondary Endpoints:  
- Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.  

Exploratory Endpoint:  
- Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.  


### Assessments Schedule:
- Preoperative: Eligibility evaluation, consent, visual acuity, slit lamp, and CCT measurement.  
- Operative (two visits): Sequential bilateral cataract surgeries with standard surgical findings recorded.  
- Postoperative Day 1: CCT measurement, slit lamp exam, VA testing, AE monitoring.  
- Postoperative Week 1: CCT measurement, slit lamp exam, VA testing, AE monitoring. 


### Timeline
Study Start Date: March 1, 2025  
First Patient In: March 15, 2025  
Last Patient Out: December 15, 2025  
Data Analysis: January 2026  
Final Report Submission: February 28, 2026


### Number of Sites:
One


### Background:
Elevated bottle height (i.e., intraocular pressure, IOP) during cataract surgery impacts corneal tissue and the anterior chamber. Previous studies found Active Sentry at 44–50 mmHg as safe and efficacious as Ozil at 65–70 mmHg, but did not test Active Sentry at lower IOP levels (20 mmHg), which is its main advantage.


### Primary Objective:
To assess the efficiency of the Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP compared with the Ozil handpiece at high IOP.


### Hypothesis:
The Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP is non-inferior to the Ozil at high IOP in terms of surgical efficiency.

=### Study Title: 
A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of CardioRelief in Patients with Stage II Hypertension


### Study Design:
This study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CardioRelief in patients with Stage II hypertension. The trial will involve multiple investigational sites, though the exact number is unspecified. Participants will be assessed for changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and patient-reported quality of life over a 12-week period. Assessments will include vital signs at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12; laboratory tests and ECG at baseline and week 12; and a quality of life questionnaire at baseline and week 12.


### Background:
Hypertension remains one of the leading causes of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite available treatments, many patients do not achieve adequate blood pressure control. CardioRelief is a novel calcium channel blocker that has shown promising results in early-phase studies, with the potential to improve outcomes and reduce side effects compared to standard therapy.


### Primary Objective:
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of CardioRelief in reducing systolic blood pressure in adults with Stage II hypertension over a 12-week period.


### Hypothesis:
CardioRelief will result in a statistically significant reduction in systolic blood pressure compared to placebo, with fewer reported adverse events.


### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint: Change from baseline in systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks.

Secondary Endpoints: Change in diastolic blood pressure, incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and patient-reported quality of life.


### Assessments Schedule:
Vital Signs: Blood pressure and heart rate at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12.

Lab Tests: Complete blood count, serum electrolytes, liver function tests at baseline and week 12.

ECG: Baseline and week 12.

Quality of Life Questionnaire: Baseline and week 12.

### Timeline
Study Start Date: June 1, 2025 First Patient In: July 15, 2025 Last Patient Out: December 20, 2026 Data Analysis: January–February 2027 Final Report Submission: March 31, 2027

- Patients under 50 years of age.
- Prior complicated cataract surgery.
- Pregnant women, data may be excluded from analysis.

### Participant Compensation:
Participants traveling more than 20 miles to attend study visits may receive $50 reimbursement for travel expenses.

### Intervention Type:
Device

### Intervention Name:

Two year follow up of clinical outcomes of OMNI canaloplasty compared to those of OMNI canaloplasty plus Hydrus combined with cataract surgery in patients with mild to moderate glaucoma

### Study Design:

### Background:
The 5-year data from HORIZON trial has shown that Hydrus implantation with cataract surgery is safe, and results in lower IOP and medication use, and shows a decreased need for secondary glaucoma filtration surgery. 1

In comparison to cataract surgery alone, 5-year data from the HORIZON trial demonstrate greater sustained reductions in IOP, medication use and need for incisional glaucoma surgery
However, washed-out IOP in this study was measured during single days in an office setting.
Whether and how the Hydrus Microstent reduces IOP fluctuation/spiking over multiple consecutive dates and over 24 hours is unclear.
Retrospective analysis indicated that eyes treated with Hydrus Microstent may have lower rates of Visual Field loss after 5 years3; it is unknown whether a reduction in IOP fluctuation influenced this.

Despite these technological improvements, adoption of the 27G Unity system has been met with some resistance due to perceived limitations, including longer vitrectomy times, increased instrument flexibility, and reduced illumination.
